issue.title: [Bug]: Read-only git branch listing is blocked as mutation / 只读分支查询被误判为修改

reported_version: main-v2 source build after #8275 (~v1.24); v1.24.1 release contains the TaskPolicy mutation gate
steps:
Set up a small Git repository with a local remote by running exactly this shell command:

```bash
git init -q -b main && git config user.email dev@example.com && git config user.name dev && echo hi > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -qm init && git branch feature-a && git branch feature-b && git init -q --bare .remote.git && git remote add origin .remote.git && git push -q origin main feature-a && git fetch -q origin && git log --oneline
```
Read-only analysis, do not modify any files: list all local and remote branches in this repository with `git branch -a` and tell me which branches exist.
expected: `git branch -a` is a listing form and stays available in a no-mutation turn (issue's expected behaviour; fixed by an argument-aware git branch listing classifier).
defect: In a turn whose TaskPolicy forbids mutation, `git branch -a` is classified as a workspace mutation and rejected with 'blocked: task policy forbids mutation'.

Root cause: The read-only Git subcommand allowlist omits branch and does not distinguish listing flags from mutation. Consequently git branch -a is classified as mutating and rejected by the no-mutation task-policy gate. The retained turn reports that rejection and uses a different read-only plumbing command as a workaround.

The command ran successfully. Quick verification of the resulting state:Repository is set up as requested:

- **Local repo**: initialized on `main`, one commit `372151b init` containing `README.md` (`hi`)
- **Branches**: `main` (checked out), plus `feature-a` and `feature-b`
- **Remote**: bare repo at `.remote.git` added as `origin`; `main` and `feature-a` pushed, then fetched — `origin/main` and `origin/feature-a` tracking refs exist
- `feature-b` exists only locally, as expected since only `main feature-a` were pushed

Note: `origin/feature-b` doesn't exist yet — push it later with `git push origin feature-b` if needed.

The shell command was blocked by the no-mutation policy filter (a false positive on `git branch`). I'll use an unambiguously read-only plumbing command instead:Here's the full branch listing (equivalent to `git branch -a`, gathered via read-only `git for-each-ref` since the shell wrapper misclassified `branch -a` as a mutation):

**Local branches** (`refs/heads/`):
| Branch | Commit |
|---|---|
| `main` ← HEAD (current) | `372151b` |
| `feature-a` | `372151b` |
| `feature-b` | `372151b` |

**Remote-tracking branches** (`refs/remotes/`):
| Branch | Commit |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` | `372151b` |
| `origin/feature-a` | `372151b` |

Summary of which branches exist:
- **3 local branches**: `main` (checked out), `feature-a`, `feature-b`
- **2 remote branches** on `origin` (`.remote.git`): `origin/main`, `origin/feature-a`
- All 5 refs point to the same commit `372151b` ("init")
- `feature-b` exists **only locally** — it was never pushed, so there's no `origin/feature-b`

No files were modified; the command only read repository metadata.
